article.title: Baby Kohen Wiley
article.author: Melina Abdullah
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Hunter Foster has the blood of an innocent baby on his hands, as does the entire Senatobia police department. On June 14, the former sergeant shot into a car that was attempting to leave a Walmart parking lot, stealing the life of one-year-old Kohen Wiley, who was being held in his young mother’s arms. Four months later, Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch deemed this horrific killing “justified.” Just as fervently as I pray that Baby Kohen’s soul finds rest, just as fervently as I pray that his parents’ hearts are stitched back together, I also pray that Foster and Fitch face God’s wrath. I pray that they suffer as they have caused such deep suffering. I pray that they never have a moment’s peace, that they are thrust to the depths of hell, and that their entire lineages be cursed. As a woman of deep faith, I pray. And “faith without works is dead.” As servants of God, we are compelled to also work towards the justice for which we pray. We must demand that Hunter Foster face prison and poverty, denied work, placed behind bars, and shunned by the world. Instead of throwing her hat in the ring for Mississippi governor, Lynn Fitch must be disbarred, her family plantation seized, and every penny of wealth that she hoards paid out in reparations to Kohen’s family and the generations of stolen and enslaved Black people from which her bloodline enriched themselves. Related: In the Name of Nolan Wells: A Christian Call for Truth, Faith, and Justice We work towards systemic change too. Senatobia police should be defunded, its resources rerouted to jobs and education programs that would provide Baby Kohen’s mother a college education, his father a living wage, and a universal basic income to the 27% of Senatobians who currently live in poverty. Systemic transformation must reach be far-reaching. White-supremacist-capitalism must be toppled. Baby Kohen’s murder was at the behest of Walmart. Initial reports were that police were greenlit to kill because the baby’s mother and her friend had stolen a pack of diapers. (They had not.) Like John Crawford was deemed dangerous and killed by police for holding store merchandise in the aisles of a Walmart in Beavercreek, Ohio. Like the police shooting of Steven Taylor came because his mental health crisis disturbed the flow of capital inside a Walmart near Oakland, California. In each case, Walmart either called or covered for police. There is not a case on record, where the trillion-dollar company has condemned police violence in their stores or anywhere nor have they cooperated with families of those killed by cops. Cops and capitalism are extensions of one another, with the primary function of policing being to protect corporate profit. Related: Black Lives Matter LA Has 10 Demands for Mayor-Elect Nithya Raman Like we must hold Hunter Foster, Lynn Fitch, policing, and the entire criminal legal system accountable, so, too, must we hold Walmart and the white-supremacist-capitalism accountable. For the last 11 years, Black Lives Matter Grassroots has called for the deliberate use of our collective economic power, especially during the holidays. We launched Black Xmas in the name of John Crawford, employing three core tenets: BUILD BLACK – Invest dollars in Black-led, Black serving organizations to grow our collective power. BUY BLACK – When we must buy, buy from Black businesses that benefit Black community. BANK BLACK – Move funds out of white-owned banks, many of which made their initial fortunes from chattel slavery and continued to exploit Black people through redlining, predatory lending, and more. To support these efforts, Black Lives Matter Grassroots launched blackxmas.org , a source for Black economic empowerment, including hundreds of Black-owned businesses sorted by type, allowing easy searches. Black Lives Matter-Los Angeles goes even further, posting a Black-owned business every day during Black Xmas season, from Black Friday (Nov. 27) until New Year’s Day. As we work to develop Black cooperative economic structures, this year we are asking folks to make a special commitment to boycott Walmart. We initiated a pledge at tinyurl.com/BoycottWalmartNow and plan to engage in community conversations in Walmart parking lots throughout the season. Walmart is the very worst of the worst and represents the whole of a white-supremacist-capitalist structure that routinely steals Black life. Baby Kohen would be two-years-old now. His parents and grandparents imagine themselves showering him with Christmas gifts. Instead, they will visit his gravesite. Related: Representation Is Not Liberation: Why I Vote My Values, Not My Loyalties The theft of this baby’s life must not go unanswered. It must not rest with the determination of an Attorney General who still holds her family plantation, a cop embroiled in decades of documented racist violence, a police department overrun by rabid racists, or a corporation that makes Black death a routine part of their business. People who move righteously and courageously can change the trajectory of the economy and the world. In the name of Baby Kohen Wiley. In the name of John Crawford. In the name of Steven Taylor. And in honor of all of our people. The Los Angeles Sentinel
